note: Complete public scientific-checker bank. Inactive unless SCIBENCH_TRIGGER_LOG is set.

checkers.alarm: max(abs(L.matrix - reciprocal(reciprocal(L)).matrix)) exceeds 100*eps64*cond(L.matrix)*max(1,|L.matrix|_inf)
checkers.invariant: reciprocal(reciprocal(L)) == L (up to numerical tolerance and the 2*pi convention factor)
checkers.observation_point: inside the reciprocal_lattice property, a re-call sanitizer computes the double application inline and compares to the original matrix
checkers.precondition: any non-degenerate lattice (volume > 0, three lattice vectors linearly independent)
checkers.rationale: the reciprocal lattice is used throughout the codebase (diffraction, k-point paths, Ewald summation, Brillouin-zone construction); if the forward/backward transform pair are not mutual inverses for some lattice, any downstream reciprocal-space computation built by round-tripping through direct space would be silently wrong for that lattice class
checkers.scientific_quantity: reciprocal lattice of a crystal's reciprocal lattice

checkers.alarm: max(abs(G1 - G2)) exceeds 100*eps64*max(lengths)^2
checkers.invariant: Lattice.from_parameters(*lat.parameters).metric_tensor is close to lat.metric_tensor for any lattice lat
checkers.observation_point: inside the metric_tensor property, a re-call sanitizer reconstructs a fresh Lattice via from_parameters(*self.parameters) and compares metric tensors
checkers.precondition: any lattice constructed directly from a matrix or via from_parameters with a non-degenerate shape: every pair of lattice vectors must have sin(angle) >= 1e-6, since the (a,b,c,alpha,beta,gamma) description cannot encode smaller angles in float64
checkers.rationale: from_parameters is the standard entry point for constructing a lattice from experimentally reported unit cell parameters; if the lengths/angles extraction or from_parameters reconstruction has any sign or formula error for some region of angle-space, every downstream geometric computation for lattices built this way would silently describe the wrong physical cell shape
checkers.scientific_quantity: metric tensor G = A A^T of a lattice, as two equivalent descriptions (matrix vs. (a,b,c,alpha,beta,gamma) sextuple) of the same lattice shape

checkers.alarm: abs(vol_before - vol_after) exceeds 100*eps64*vol_before*max(1, cond(L)), where cond(L) is the 2-norm condition number of the input lattice matrix
checkers.invariant: abs(lat.get_lll_reduced_lattice().volume - lat.volume) < tol
checkers.observation_point: inside get_lll_reduced_lattice, comparing volume before and after reduction
checkers.precondition: any non-degenerate lattice, delta in the standard LLL parameter range (default 0.75)
checkers.rationale: LLL reduction is used pervasively as a preprocessing step (Niggli reduction explicitly reduces via LLL first) precisely because it is assumed to be a lossless change of basis; a volume-changing 'reduction' would mean the returned lattice is not actually equivalent to the input, silently corrupting every quantity computed from it downstream
checkers.scientific_quantity: lattice covolume (unit cell volume) under LLL basis reduction, an integer unimodular change of basis

checkers.alarm: max(abs(f - roundtrip(f))) exceeds 100*eps64*cond(lll_mapping)*max(1,magnitude(f))
checkers.invariant: get_frac_coords_from_lll(get_lll_frac_coords(f)) == f for any fractional coordinate f
checkers.observation_point: inside get_lll_frac_coords, a re-call sanitizer composes with get_frac_coords_from_lll (via lll_mapping directly) and compares to the input
checkers.precondition: any non-degenerate lattice, any fractional coordinate (including outside [0,1), since this is a pure linear transform, not a periodic-image reduction)
checkers.rationale: get_lll_frac_coords is used internally for periodic-image search and coordinate wrapping in reduced-basis space; a broken round-trip would mean fractional coordinates silently drift when passed through the LLL basis, corrupting any distance or neighbor computation that relies on this transform pair
checkers.scientific_quantity: fractional coordinates converted into the LLL-reduced basis and back, via lll_inverse/lll_mapping being genuine matrix inverses of each other

checkers.alarm: abs(d_metric - d_vector) exceeds 100*eps64*max(abs(hkl))*d_metric*max(1,cond(G*))
checkers.invariant: d_hkl(hkl) is close to 1/norm(hkl @ reciprocal_lattice_crystallographic.matrix)
checkers.observation_point: inside d_hkl, a re-call sanitizer computes the alternate vector-norm form and compares
checkers.precondition: any non-degenerate lattice, any nonzero integer Miller index (h,k,l)
checkers.rationale: d_hkl underlies diffraction pattern simulation (Bragg's law uses d_hkl directly to predict peak positions); a formula inconsistency for some lattice/Miller-index combination would silently mispredict diffraction angles for that class of crystal
checkers.scientific_quantity: spacing between adjacent (hkl) lattice planes, computed two independent ways: metric-tensor quadratic form vs. reciprocal-vector-norm

checkers.alarm: (comp*k).reduced_formula != comp.reduced_formula (exact string equality, tol=0)
checkers.invariant: (comp * k).reduced_formula == comp.reduced_formula for any positive integer k
checkers.observation_point: inside reduced_formula, a re-call sanitizer scales the composition by k and re-derives the reduced formula on the scaled copy, comparing strings
checkers.precondition: any Composition whose amounts are comfortably (100x) inside amount_tolerance (1e-8) of an integer AND comfortably (100x) below float64's exact-integer ceiling (2**53), any positive integer scaling factor k in {2,3,5}, excluding special_formulas overrides (e.g. peroxides) which the code intentionally does not fully reduce
checkers.rationale: formula reduction is used throughout pymatgen (deduplication, phase-diagram grouping by reduced composition, materials database keys); if reduction were not actually scale-invariant for some composition, two representations of the same physical substance would silently be treated as chemically distinct
checkers.scientific_quantity: chemical formula identity under uniform scaling of stoichiometric coefficients by a positive factor

checkers.alarm: (when the precondition holds) abs(sum(fractions) - 1) exceeds 100*eps64*n_elements (n_elements = len(comp.elements))
checkers.invariant: sum over distinct element symbols of the atomic fraction == 1 within tolerance; get_atomic_fraction(Element) is the symbol aggregate (sums every Species of that symbol), so a bare Element key and a Species key of the same symbol are counted once
checkers.observation_point: inside get_atomic_fraction, a re-call sanitizer (guarded against recursion) sums the fraction with one term per distinct symbol (the aggregate if a bare Element key is present, else the per-Species terms) and compares to 1, the first time it is called for a composition
checkers.precondition: any non-empty Composition (num_atoms > 0) in which no symbol mixes a bare Element key with Species keys of opposite sign (their signed aggregate would cancel while num_atoms sums |amount| per key); the stored amounts must sum (in absolute value) to the accumulated atom count, which excludes constructor input with colliding keys such as {'Fe': 1, Element('Fe'): 2}
checkers.rationale: atomic fractions are used directly in phase-diagram composition-space coordinates and in reporting stoichiometry to users; a partition violation would mean the reported fractions do not actually describe a valid decomposition of the whole composition, for example when a composition mixes oxidation-state-labeled and unlabeled entries for the same element
checkers.scientific_quantity: atomic fractions of all elements in a composition, which must partition the whole (sum to exactly 1)

checkers.alarm: max element-wise diff exceeds 100*eps64*n_elements
checkers.invariant: Composition.from_weight_dict(comp.as_weight_dict()).fractional_composition is close to comp.fractional_composition
checkers.observation_point: inside as_weight_dict, a re-call sanitizer composes with from_weight_dict and compares the resulting fractional_composition to the original
checkers.precondition: any Composition with at least one Element-keyed (not Species-keyed -- as_weight_dict/from_weight_dict do not support oxidation-state-labeled species) present element, and no present element within 100x of Composition.amount_tolerance of its own mole fraction, and stored amounts that sum (in absolute value) to the accumulated atom count (no colliding duplicate keys in the constructor input)
checkers.rationale: from_weight_dict/from_weights exist specifically to let users specify alloy/industrial compositions in weight percent; a round-trip failure would mean the atomic composition pymatgen derives from a weight-percent specification does not actually correspond to the weight percent the user intended, silently mislabeling the material's stoichiometry
checkers.scientific_quantity: weight fraction and atomic fraction as two mutually-invertible representations of the same chemical composition, related by each element's atomic mass

checkers.alarm: any symbol's amount differing by more than 100*eps64*max(1, largest absolute amount among the operands, the pooled sum and the result), after removing the per-key amounts below amount_tolerance that the constructor drops
checkers.invariant: (c1+c2).get_el_amt_dict() equals the dict obtained by independently pooling c1.get_el_amt_dict() and c2.get_el_amt_dict() key-by-key; a merged per-key amount with |amount| below Composition.amount_tolerance, which the constructor drops by design (e.g. allow_negative cancellation residue), is removed from the pooled sum
checkers.observation_point: inside __add__, a re-call sanitizer independently pools both operands' get_el_amt_dict() and compares to the result's own get_el_amt_dict()
checkers.precondition: any two compositions c1, c2 with matching allow_negative
checkers.rationale: Composition.__add__ is the primary mechanism for combining reaction products/reactants and for building up compositions programmatically; a species/symbol pooling inconsistency would most plausibly indicate a bug in how oxidation-state-labeled species are merged when their labels differ but their underlying element is the same, silently under- or over-counting an element's total amount
checkers.scientific_quantity: composition addition at the Species-resolved level (__add__'s own representation) vs. addition at the symbol-pooled level (get_el_amt_dict's representation)

checkers.alarm: max(abs(point - roundtrip)) exceeds 100*eps64*cond(affine_matrix)*max(1,norm(point))
checkers.invariant: op.inverse.operate(op.operate(point)) is close to point for any Cartesian point
checkers.observation_point: inside operate, a re-call sanitizer (guarded against recursion) composes with .inverse.operate and compares to the original point
checkers.precondition: any SymmOp whose affine_matrix is invertible (det(rotation_matrix) != 0)
checkers.rationale: SymmOp.inverse is used to map transformed structures back to a reference frame (e.g. in symmetry-based structure comparison and Wyckoff-position assignment); a broken inverse for some construction path would silently misplace atoms when un-applying a symmetry operation, without any error being raised
checkers.scientific_quantity: affine transformation and its inverse composing to the identity for any invertible SymmOp

checkers.alarm: max(abs(R @ R.T - eye(3))) exceeds 100*eps64
checkers.invariant: allclose(R @ R.T, eye(3)) for the constructed rotation_matrix
checkers.observation_point: inside from_axis_angle_and_translation, immediately after assembling the Rodrigues-formula rotation matrix, before delegating to from_rotation_and_translation
checkers.precondition: any SymmOp constructed via from_axis_angle_and_translation, for any rotation axis whose squared norm is a finite normal float64 (at least finfo.tiny/eps64 and at most finfo.max), so that axis / norm(axis) is computed without underflow or overflow, and any angle
checkers.rationale: every consumer of a SymmOp constructed this way implicitly assumes the rotation part is a genuine rotation; a non-orthogonal rotation matrix would silently distort distances and angles under operate/operate_multi, corrupting every symmetry-based structure comparison built on it
checkers.scientific_quantity: proper rotation matrix (R @ R.T == I), the defining algebraic property of the orthogonal group O(3)

checkers.alarm: max(abs(batch_result - single_stack)) exceeds 100*eps64*max(1,max absolute sum of affine dot-product terms)
checkers.invariant: op.operate_multi(points)[i] is close to op.operate(points[i]) for every i
checkers.observation_point: inside operate_multi, a re-call sanitizer (guarded against recursion) compares against per-point operate() calls
checkers.precondition: any SymmOp, any finite set of Cartesian points
checkers.rationale: operate_multi is the performance path used whenever a symmetry operation is applied to an entire structure's worth of sites at once; a batch/single discrepancy would mean bulk structure transformations silently disagree with the single-point semantics SymmOp.operate defines
checkers.scientific_quantity: applying a fixed affine transformation to a batch of points (via np.inner) vs. one at a time (via np.dot)

checkers.alarm: n_electrons != atomic_number (tol=0)
checkers.invariant: element.n_electrons == element.Z (exact integer equality)
checkers.observation_point: inside ElementBase.n_electrons (the neutral-atom class only, not Species's own separate n_electrons)
checkers.precondition: any Element(symbol) for any of the 118 supported elements, in its neutral (non-ionized) Element form (Species, which has a nonzero oxi_state, is a separate class not covered by this precondition)
checkers.rationale: full_electronic_structure and n_electrons are used for electronic-structure-based analyses (term symbol derivation, valence electron counting for bonding models); a mismatch for any of the 118 elements would indicate a data-entry error in that element's stored configuration string, silently producing wrong valence-electron counts, term symbols, and derived chemistry for that specific element across every downstream analysis
checkers.scientific_quantity: electron count of a neutral atom, cross-checked via summing full_electronic_structure's subshells against the stored atomic number Z

checkers.alarm: any term symbol with J outside [|L-S|, L+S] (tol=1e-9 for float rounding in the bounds arithmetic only)
checkers.invariant: for every term symbol produced by term_symbols, the parsed J satisfies abs(L-S) <= J <= L+S
checkers.observation_point: inside term_symbols, after the full combinatorial term enumeration, parsing every generated string and checking the triangle inequality against the parsed L, S
checkers.precondition: any non-noble-gas element with a resolvable electronic_structure (a handful of superheavy elements and elements with 'ambiguous valence' per the library's own ValueError raise naturally have no term_symbols to check)
checkers.rationale: term symbols are used to identify spectroscopic states and (via ground_state_term_symbol) to determine Hund's-rule ground states for magnetic moment and valence predictions; a term outside the allowed J range would be physically meaningless and would indicate a defect in the underlying combinatorial term-enumeration algorithm
checkers.scientific_quantity: total angular momentum quantum number J for Russell-Saunders term-symbol coupling, bounded by the triangle inequality |L-S| <= J <= L+S

checkers.alarm: len(supercell) != len(original)*round(abs(det(M))) (tol=0, exact integer count)
checkers.invariant: len(struct.make_supercell(M)) == len(original) * round(abs(det(M))) exactly
checkers.observation_point: inside make_supercell, after the supercell is built, comparing site counts
checkers.precondition: any Structure with n sites, any integer 3x3 scaling matrix M with det(M) a positive integer
checkers.rationale: every physical property computed from a supercell (total energy per formula unit, density, composition) implicitly assumes the site count scaled correctly with the chosen supercell size; a silent site-count error would corrupt every such downstream computation without raising any error
checkers.scientific_quantity: site count of a supercell built with integer scaling matrix M (det(M)=N), which must be exactly N times the original site count

checkers.alarm: abs(supercell.volume - original.volume*abs(det(M))) exceeds 100*eps64*original.volume*abs(det(M))*max(1, cond), where cond is the larger 2-norm condition number of the original and supercell lattice matrices
checkers.invariant: struct.make_supercell(M).volume is close to struct.volume * abs(det(M))
checkers.observation_point: inside make_supercell, alongside PM-STR-001, comparing volumes
checkers.precondition: same as PM-STR-001
checkers.rationale: density and any per-unit-volume property computed on a supercell directly divides by volume; a volume/determinant mismatch would silently produce a wrong density or per-volume quantity for structures built via make_supercell, without the site-count law (PM-STR-001) necessarily catching it
checkers.scientific_quantity: volume of a supercell built with scaling matrix M, which is det(M) times the original cell's volume (the determinant's geometric meaning as a volume-scaling factor)

checkers.alarm: abs(density - mass_g/volume_cm3) exceeds 100*eps64*density
checkers.invariant: struct.density is close to (mass in grams)/(volume in cm^3), independently re-derived rather than reading density's own cached computation path
checkers.observation_point: inside density, a re-call sanitizer independently re-derives mass_g and volume_cm3 via Mass/Length unit objects and compares
checkers.precondition: any Structure with at least one site and a non-degenerate lattice
checkers.rationale: density is a commonly reported and compared materials property; a unit-conversion error in the Angstrom-to-cm cubic scaling (an easy off-by-10^24-class mistake, since volume converts as length-cubed) would silently produce a density wrong by a large, systematic factor for every structure
checkers.scientific_quantity: mass density as mass per unit volume, combining Composition.weight (periodic-table atomic-mass sums) and Lattice.volume (geometric determinant) via a unit-conversion chain

checkers.alarm: abs(dist - recomputed_dist) exceeds 100*eps64*max_lattice_length*max(1,abs(jimage)+abs(f1)+abs(f2))
checkers.invariant: dist returned by get_distance_and_image(f1,f2) is close to norm(get_cartesian_coords(jimage+f2-f1)) for the same jimage the function returned
checkers.observation_point: inside get_distance_and_image, a re-call sanitizer recomputes the distance from the returned jimage via get_cartesian_coords and compares
checkers.precondition: any non-degenerate lattice with cond(matrix) < 1e4, any two fractional coordinates, the jimage=None (nearest-image-search) branch only
checkers.rationale: jimage is consumed downstream to identify which periodic bond/neighbor is being referred to (e.g. in bonding graphs); a distance/image mismatch would mean the reported image does not actually correspond to the reported distance, silently mislabeling which periodic neighbor a given bond distance refers to
checkers.scientific_quantity: minimum periodic-boundary distance between two fractional coordinates and the jimage translation that achieves it, which must be mutually consistent per the function's own documented contract

checkers.alarm: e_above_hull < -100*numerical_tol (the class's own numerical_tol constant, examined per SANITIZER.md 5.8 T rather than assumed correct for this new quantity)
checkers.invariant: get_e_above_hull(entry) >= -tol for any entry in qhull_entries
checkers.observation_point: inside get_decomp_and_e_above_hull, at the computation of e_above_hull, restricted to entries in qhull_entries, before the existing raise/accept branch
checkers.precondition: any entry that is one of the PhaseDiagram's own qhull_entries (not an arbitrary external entry being tested against an existing hull), called with allow_negative=False (the default)
checkers.rationale: e_above_hull is the single most widely used stability metric in materials screening; a hull-defining entry computing as below its own hull would indicate a genuine defect in the Qhull facet-matching or the chemical-potential linear solve, silently producing physically impossible negative-stability values
checkers.scientific_quantity: energy above the convex hull of formation energies, which by the defining property of a convex hull cannot be negative for any entry that was part of the hull's own construction (qhull_entries)

checkers.alarm: abs(sum-1) exceeds 100*eps64*(dim+1)*max(1, cond) (cond = 2-norm condition number of the facet simplex's augmented vertex matrix, from which the barycentric coordinates are solved), or any amount < -10*PhaseDiagram.numerical_tol
checkers.invariant: sum(get_decomposition(comp).values()) is close to 1, and every value is >= -tol
checkers.observation_point: inside get_decomposition, summing the raw (pre-filter) barycentric coordinates and checking the minimum
checkers.precondition: any composition within the phase diagram's convex hull in composition space (a facet is found without raising RuntimeError)
checkers.rationale: get_decomposition's output is used directly to compute the hull energy (a weighted sum using these exact amounts as weights) and to report reaction products/stoichiometry to users; amounts that do not sum to 1 would mean the reported decomposition does not actually balance the original composition
checkers.scientific_quantity: decomposition amounts (barycentric coordinates within the containing facet's simplex), which by definition must be non-negative and sum to exactly 1

checkers.alarm: any element's amount differing by more than 100*eps64*(dim+1)*max(1, cond) + Composition.amount_tolerance (cond as in PM-PD-002) between the reconstructed and original fractional composition
checkers.invariant: sum(amt * entry.composition.fractional_composition for entry, amt in get_decomposition(comp).items()) is close to comp.fractional_composition
checkers.observation_point: inside get_decomposition, alongside PM-PD-002, reconstructing the weighted composition sum
checkers.precondition: same as PM-PD-002, on the composition's fractional form; the target fractional composition is stored at Composition.amount_tolerance resolution (components below it are dropped by the constructor); the composition's stored amounts must sum (in absolute value) to its accumulated atom count (no colliding duplicate keys in the constructor input)
checkers.rationale: this is the property that makes a 'decomposition' chemically meaningful at all; a facet/amount misalignment bug would silently report a chemically inconsistent reaction while both individual amounts and their sum-to-1 property (PM-PD-002) looked entirely correct -- an independent cross-check from PM-PD-002, since it additionally depends on the facet vertices being correctly indexed and aligned with the barycentric coordinates
checkers.scientific_quantity: decomposition amounts weighted by the facet vertex entries' own compositions, which must recombine to the original composition (the mass-conservation law underlying any phase decomposition)

checkers.alarm: abs(e1 - e2) exceeds max(100*10^-acc_factor,1000*eps64)*max(1,|e1|,|e2|,T), where T is the largest absolute value among the real, reciprocal, point and charged-cell energy terms of either object
checkers.invariant: EwaldSummation(struct, eta=eta1).total_energy is close to EwaldSummation(struct, eta=eta2).total_energy for two different positive eta values
checkers.observation_point: inside total_energy, a re-call sanitizer builds a second EwaldSummation on the same structure with a different eta (10x or 1/10x the original) and compares total_energy
checkers.precondition: any structure with oxidation-state-decorated species or explicit site charges (required by compute_average_oxidation_state), any two positive eta values, each with its own eta-dependent automatic real_space_cut/recip_space_cut
checkers.rationale: eta is explicitly documented as a free performance-tuning knob with little effect on the total energy; if the total energy is not actually invariant to eta for some structure class, the library's own stated contract would be false for that structure, silently producing an eta-dependent (i.e. non-physical) energy that downstream code (e.g. EwaldMinimizer) treats as absolute and physically meaningful
checkers.scientific_quantity: total Ewald electrostatic energy, computed with two different eta real/reciprocal split parameters (each with its own eta-dependent auto cutoffs) on the same structure

checkers.alarm: any neighbor present in one function's output set and absent from the other's (index/image/rounded-distance mismatch)
checkers.invariant: for each site i, the SET of (neighbor_index, jimage, round(distance,6)) triples from get_all_neighbors(r)[i] equals the set from get_all_neighbors_old(r, include_index=True, include_image=True)[i], compared order-independently
checkers.observation_point: a re-call sanitizer wrapping get_all_neighbors, additionally invoking get_all_neighbors_old on the same structure/cutoff and comparing per-site neighbor sets
checkers.precondition: any Structure with at least one site and a non-degenerate lattice, any cutoff radius r > 0, gated to len(structure)*r <= 200 to keep the O(supercell_size*n_sites) oracle affordable during ordinary test runs (a problem-size precondition, not a restriction of the underlying law); neighbors at distance <= 1e-8 (coincident distinct sites, which the brute-force oracle drops by convention) are excluded from both sets
checkers.rationale: get_all_neighbors is the primary, performance-optimized entry point used throughout the codebase (coordination-number analysis, bonding graphs, local-environment fingerprints); a systematic disagreement with the author-maintained brute-force oracle would mean the fast path silently misses or fabricates neighbors for some structure class
checkers.scientific_quantity: set of periodic neighbors within a cutoff radius r of every site, computed via the fast vectorized get_neighbor_list path vs. the author-declared brute-force oracle get_all_neighbors_old (explicitly decorated 'retained purely for checking purposes')

checkers.alarm: any neighbor present in one function's output set and absent from the other's, outside the boundary-exclusion band
checkers.invariant: for each site i, the SET of (neighbor_index, jimage, round(distance,6)) triples from get_all_neighbors_py(r)[i] equals the set from get_all_neighbors_old(r, ...)[i], restricted to neighbors unambiguously inside or outside the cutoff (see precondition FIX)
checkers.observation_point: a re-call sanitizer wrapping get_all_neighbors_py, invoking get_all_neighbors_old on the same structure/cutoff and comparing per-site neighbor sets
checkers.precondition: same as PM-STR-005, plus: entries whose neighbor distance falls within max(numerical_tol, 5e-7) of the cutoff r are excluded from the fast/old set comparison, since get_points_in_spheres pads the cutoff by numerical_tol and the oracle does not
checkers.rationale: get_all_neighbors_py's docstring positions it as an alternative implementation of the same neighbor-search contract; localizing a defect to the KD-tree path specifically (rather than get_neighbor_list) gives independent coverage of both non-deprecated neighbor-search entry points
checkers.scientific_quantity: same law as PM-STR-005, exercised through a third, independently-implemented algorithm: get_all_neighbors_py's KD-tree-based get_points_in_spheres spatial search, cross-checked against the same get_all_neighbors_old brute-force oracle

checkers.alarm: max periodic-image residual (in Cartesian Angstrom) across all (op, site) pairs exceeds max(10*symprec, 100*eps64)
checkers.invariant: for every returned SymmOp op and every site s, op applied to s's fractional coordinates lands (modulo np.round of the fractional difference) within tolerance of some site of the same species
checkers.observation_point: a re-call sanitizer inside get_symmetry_operations (fractional-coordinate branch only), checking every (op, site) pair's periodic atom correspondence against the full site list
checkers.precondition: any Structure for which SpacegroupAnalyzer succeeds (_get_symmetry does not raise), any operation in get_symmetry_operations()'s returned list, evaluated with periodic (minimum-image) matching; gated to len(structure)*n_ops <= 5000 for affordability
checkers.rationale: every downstream consumer of get_symmetry_operations() (symmetrized structures, Wyckoff-position assignment, symmetry-based structure comparison) implicitly trusts each returned operation is a genuine symmetry of the structure; a spglib-interface bug (e.g. in the fractional-translation rationalization step) could silently return an operation that does not actually map the structure onto itself
checkers.scientific_quantity: physical correspondence of every spglib-sourced periodic symmetry operation: applying the operation to every site's fractional coordinates must map it (modulo lattice translation) onto a site of the same species -- the periodic-boundary-aware analogue of PointGroupAnalyzer.is_valid_op's existing molecular-case check, freshly implemented here since is_valid_op has no periodic awareness

checkers.alarm: abs(trace(T)-trace(T_rot)) exceeds 100*(eps64*scale + scale*max(ortho_err,eps64)), where scale = max(1, |trace|, max|T|), or the analogous eigenvalue-max-deviation bound (scale = max(1, max|eig|, max|T|)), where ortho_err is R's own measured (R@R.T-I) max deviation
checkers.invariant: trace(tensor.rotate(R)) is close to trace(tensor), and sorted(eigvalsh(tensor.rotate(R))) is close to sorted(eigvalsh(tensor)), for any R accepted by rotate's own precondition
checkers.observation_point: a re-call sanitizer wrapping Tensor.rotate, independently recomputing trace via np.trace and eigenvalues via np.linalg.eigvalsh on both the input and rotated tensors, and recording R's own orthogonality deviation (R@R.T - I)
checkers.precondition: any rank-2 (3x3) Tensor, any rotation matrix accepted by SquareTensor.is_rotation(tol) for whatever tol the caller supplies to rotate() (the library's own validity check, reused as-is -- NOT restricted to machine-precision-exact orthogonality, since rotate's own tol parameter documents that approximately-orthogonal matrices are a valid input); real or complex rank-2 tensors (eigenvalues are taken of the Hermitian part (T + T^H)/2, which is rotation-invariant for real R)
checkers.rationale: Tensor.rotate/transform are used to re-express measured or computed physical-property tensors (elastic constants, piezoelectric tensors, dielectric tensors) in a different crystallographic frame; a bug in the congruence transform would silently distort the physical content of the tensor for some rotation
checkers.scientific_quantity: trace and (sorted) eigenvalues of a rank-2 tensor, invariant under a proper-rotation congruence transform -- a standard similarity-invariance fact of linear algebra, independent of SymmOp.transform_tensor's einsum-based implementation

checkers.alarm: abs(1 - abs(cos_angle_between_the_two_normals)) exceeds 100*eps64*max(1,cond(reciprocal_lattice.matrix))
checkers.invariant: Slab.normal is close, up to sign, to the Miller-index-derived reciprocal-lattice normal, for a Slab built with reorient_lattice=False
checkers.observation_point: at the end of get_slab, before Slab construction, comparing the raw cross-product normal of struct.lattice's first two vectors against the reciprocal-lattice-derived normal for the same miller_index
checkers.precondition: any Slab constructed by SlabGenerator.get_slab from a bulk structure and a Miller index with at least one nonzero component, WITHOUT the default lattice-reorientation post-processing (reorient_lattice=False) -- confirmed empirically that reorient_lattice=True (the default) rebuilds the lattice via Lattice.from_parameters under a fixed canonical orientation convention, which always makes Slab.normal exactly [0,0,1] in the lab frame, decoupled from the crystallographic Miller-derived direction; comparing those is not this law's subject and was confirmed (via direct testing) not a bug but a convention mismatch
checkers.rationale: the surface normal is used directly in dipole-moment calculation (Slab.dipole) and implicitly defines which direction is 'into the vacuum' for every downstream surface-science analysis; if the constructed slab's actual lattice vectors do not correspond to the Miller index the user requested, every such analysis would silently operate on the wrong crystallographic surface
checkers.scientific_quantity: surface normal derived two ways: (1) directly, as the cross product of the constructed slab's own first two (in-plane) lattice vectors, or (2) via the reciprocal lattice, as the Cartesian direction of the reciprocal lattice vector G_hkl for the requested Miller index -- a standard crystallographic fact that these must agree up to sign, analogous to the already-accepted PM-LAT-005 (d_hkl via metric tensor vs. explicit reciprocal-vector norm)
checkers.symbol: SlabGenerator.get_slab (Slab.normal vs. the Miller-index-derived reciprocal-lattice normal)

checkers.alarm: n_layers_slab != n_layers_recompute (exact integer equality, tol=0 per SANITIZER.md 5.8 X -- both are layer counts, integers by construction)
checkers.invariant: n_layers_slab (the construction-time sizing value) equals round(atom_c_span * n_layers_total) + 1 (the atom-span recomputation, with a +1 fencepost correction since n_layers_slab atomic layers span n_layers_slab-1 inter-layer gaps between the first and last atom)
checkers.observation_point: at the end of get_slab, before Slab construction, comparing the construction-time n_layers_slab against the atom-span recomputation evaluated on the slab as stacked (the structure captured before the optional lll_reduce basis change, identical to the final structure when lll_reduce=False), since after LLL the c vector is no longer the stacking vector
checkers.precondition: any Slab constructed via SlabGenerator.get_slab with primitive=False (primitive-cell reduction can change the effective layer count in a way not modeled by either formula), AND the oriented unit cell must have exactly one distinct atomic c-fractional layer (confirmed empirically: low-symmetry Miller indices like (2,1,0)/(2,1,1) can place more than one atomic layer per oriented-unit-cell repeat, breaking the 'one repeat == one layer' assumption both formulas share) -- checked at the observation point, not assumed a priori
checkers.rationale: min_slab_size/min_vac_size are the primary user-facing controls for slab thickness in surface-science workflows (surface energy convergence studies explicitly vary these); a discrepancy between the requested/computed layer count and what was actually built would mean a convergence study silently uses a different slab thickness than the one it believes it is comparing against
checkers.scientific_quantity: the number of atomic layers in a constructed slab, computed two ways: (1) a top-down sizing formula at construction time (n_layers_slab, from min_slab_size/height or min_slab_size/height_per_layer depending on in_unit_planes), and (2) a bottom-up post-construction measurement of where the atoms actually ended up (the c-fractional-coordinate span between the lowest and highest atomic layer, times the total layer count) -- the same measurement Slab.get_tasker2_slabs already performs internally for its own, unrelated purpose
checkers.symbol: SlabGenerator.get_slab (n_layers_slab vs. the atom-span-based recomputation Slab.get_tasker2_slabs already performs internally)

checkers.alarm: (k_voigt - k_reuss) < -tol or (g_voigt - g_reuss) < -tol, with tol = 100*eps64*max(1,|K or G value|)*max(1,cond(voigt))
checkers.invariant: k_voigt >= k_reuss - tol and g_voigt >= g_reuss - tol for any physically stable ElasticTensor
checkers.observation_point: inside k_vrh, gated on k_vrh>0 and g_vrh>0 (computed first, before the check runs), comparing k_voigt/k_reuss and g_voigt/g_reuss
checkers.precondition: any ElasticTensor that is physically stable (k_vrh > 0, g_vrh > 0); the Voigt matrix must additionally be symmetric (max|C-C^T| <= 1e-8 max|C|) and positive definite (Born mechanical stability) with min eigenvalue / max eigenvalue above about 1e-7, so that the eigenvalue sign is numerically reliable; outside the Born-stable domain the Voigt-Reuss bounds do not apply
checkers.rationale: k_vrh/g_vrh (the commonly reported 'the' bulk/shear modulus) implicitly assume k_voigt >= k_reuss to be a meaningful average of two bounds rather than an average of two arbitrarily-ordered numbers; a bug in the compliance-tensor inversion or Reuss aggregation formula could silently invert this ordering for some tensor
checkers.scientific_quantity: for any thermodynamically stable elastic tensor, the Voigt average (arithmetic mean, uniform-strain assumption) is a rigorous upper bound and the Reuss average (reciprocal mean of the compliance tensor, uniform-stress assumption) is a rigorous lower bound on the true polycrystalline modulus -- the Voigt-Reuss variational bounds theorem, k_voigt >= k_reuss and g_voigt >= g_reuss always

checkers.alarm: anisotropy < -tol, with tol = 100*eps64*max(1,mag)*max(1,cond(voigt)), mag = max of the four Voigt/Reuss moduli magnitudes
checkers.invariant: universal_anisotropy >= -tol for any physically stable ElasticTensor
checkers.observation_point: inside universal_anisotropy, gated on k_vrh>0 and g_vrh>0 (computed first, before the check runs)
checkers.precondition: any ElasticTensor that is physically stable (k_vrh > 0, g_vrh > 0); the Voigt matrix must additionally be symmetric (max|C-C^T| <= 1e-8 max|C|) and positive definite (Born mechanical stability) with min eigenvalue / max eigenvalue above about 1e-7, so that the eigenvalue sign is numerically reliable; outside the Born-stable domain the Voigt-Reuss bounds do not apply
checkers.rationale: universal_anisotropy is reported directly as a materials-screening descriptor; a negative value is not merely numerically surprising but physically impossible by the defining theorem, so its appearance would indicate a defect in the underlying Voigt/Reuss computation propagating into every anisotropy-based analysis or database entry built on this value
checkers.scientific_quantity: the universal anisotropy index A^U = 5*(g_voigt/g_reuss) + (k_voigt/k_reuss) - 6, defined so A^U = 0 for a perfectly isotropic material and A^U > 0 otherwise -- a direct algebraic consequence of PM-ELAST-001's same Voigt-Reuss bound theorem (each ratio >= 1)

checkers.alarm: max(abs(mod1(returned_frac - expected_frac))) exceeds 100*eps64*max(1,magnitude), where mod1(d) = d - round(d) and magnitude = max(1, max|start_coords|, max|end_coords|)
checkers.invariant: when the amplitudes contain 0, interpolate(...)[0].frac_coords equals self.frac_coords; when the last amplitude x has x*end_amplitude == 1, interpolate(...)[-1].frac_coords equals end_structure.frac_coords; both comparisons MODULO AN INTEGER LATTICE TRANSLATION (see deviation note)
checkers.observation_point: inside interpolate, after all images are constructed, comparing the first and last returned structures' fractional coordinates against self and end_structure
checkers.precondition: any two Structures interpolate accepts without raising (equal length, matching per-site species), any nimages (integer or explicit list), any pbc/autosort_tol/interpolate_lattices combination, the end-structure comparison applies only when the last amplitude x satisfies x*end_amplitude == 1 (the image equals end_structure only then; any other total amplitude interpolates to a different target by design), while the x=0 start check applies regardless of end_amplitude; the start comparison applies only when the amplitude list contains 0 (an explicit list such as [0.25, 0.5, 0.75] has no x=0 image)
checkers.rationale: interpolate is the standard construction path for NEB (nudged elastic band) reaction-pathway inputs; NEB calculations explicitly assume the first and last images ARE the reactant and product structures unmodified. A silent endpoint discrepancy (most plausibly from the autosort_tol site-matching permutation) would mean a downstream NEB calculation silently starts or ends at a slightly different structure than the one the user specified.
checkers.scientific_quantity: interpolate's x=0 and x=1 boundary images, the two endpoints of the one-parameter affine family in x it constructs, which must exactly reproduce the start and end structures (the family must pass through the two points it interpolates between)

checkers.alarm: max per-element abs(image.composition[el] - self.composition[el]) exceeds 100*eps64*max(1,n_elements)
checkers.invariant: image.composition equals self.composition for every image in interpolate(...)
checkers.observation_point: inside interpolate, after all images are constructed, comparing each image's composition against self.composition
checkers.precondition: any two Structures interpolate accepts without raising, for every value of nimages, pbc, and autosort_tol -- checked on EVERY returned image, not just the endpoints (a genuinely distinct check from PM-STR-007, which only inspects the two boundary images)
checkers.rationale: if species_and_occu's aggregation into Composition diverges from the literal per-site species list passed to type(self)(...) for some occupancy pattern (partial occupancy, disordered sites), an NEB image could silently represent a different stoichiometry than every other image in the same pathway, corrupting any energy-per-atom or per-formula-unit normalization applied across the interpolated series
checkers.scientific_quantity: every image interpolate returns must have the same chemical composition as the start structure -- atoms are not created, destroyed, or relabeled by a purely geometric coordinate interpolation

checkers.alarm: abs(weighted_sum - target_charge) exceeds 100*eps64*max(1,num_atoms)
checkers.invariant: for every solution dict sol in oxi_state_guesses(...), sum(oxi_state * comp.get_el_amt_dict()[el] for el, oxi_state in sol.items()) equals target_charge, using comp's ORIGINAL (unreduced) el_amt_dict
checkers.observation_point: inside oxi_state_guesses (the public method, after any max_sites reduction/rescaling has already happened), recomputing the weighted sum against self.get_el_amt_dict() on the original, unreduced composition
checkers.precondition: any Composition with integer atom amounts (the method's own documented restriction), any target_charge, any oxi_states_override/all_oxi_states/max_sites combination for which oxi_state_guesses returns at least one non-empty solution
checkers.rationale: add_charges_from_oxi_state_guesses and Structure.add_oxidation_state_by_guess both consume this result directly to decorate a structure's species with charges, which downstream Ewald-summation (PM-EWALD-001) and bond-valence analyses require to be genuinely charge-neutral; a max_sites-reduction rescaling bug silently hands a charged-looking but non-neutral oxidation-state assignment to exactly the electrostatic machinery that assumes neutrality
checkers.scientific_quantity: oxi_state_guesses's returned per-element average oxidation states, weighted by the ORIGINAL (pre-max_sites-reduction) composition's own atom counts, must sum to the requested target_charge -- the defining condition of charge balance

checkers.alarm: orbit_size <= 0 or len(symmetry_operations) % orbit_size != 0 (tol=0, exact integer divisibility per SANITIZER.md 5.8 X), evaluated only when the image-separation precondition holds; coincident (<=0.1*site_tolerance) and well-separated (>=10*site_tolerance) images keep the exact check; images separated by more than site_tolerance and at most 1e3*eps64 are treated as unresolved and skipped
checkers.invariant: len(self.symmetry_operations) % len(orbit_of_this_coordinate) == 0, where orbit_of_this_coordinate is computed independently per input coordinate (deduplicated only among that one coordinate's own symmetry images, not against the cross-coordinate coords_out accumulator _unique_coords itself uses for its output)
checkers.observation_point: at the end of _unique_coords's per-input-coordinate inner loop (both the magmoms and non-magmoms branches), counting how many of len(self.symmetry_operations) operations produced a distinct point for that one coordinate
checkers.precondition: any CIF whose parsed symmetry_operations genuinely form a closed group under composition (a check of the orbit-expansion arithmetic given whatever operation list self.symmetry_operations already holds, not of whether the parser correctly extracted a complete operation list from the CIF text); any starting coordinate the CIF's _atom_site_* loop supplies, provided its symmetry images are unambiguous under the parser's site_tolerance: the check is skipped when any two of the coordinate's operation images are separated (periodic, per-component maximum) by more than 0.1*site_tolerance and less than 10*site_tolerance, the band in which the greedy tolerance-based deduplication is non-transitive (coordinate within ~site_tolerance of a symmetry element); the check is also skipped when two operation images differ by more than site_tolerance yet by no more than 1e3*eps64 (images coinciding only to float64 rounding, which a tolerance below rounding level cannot merge)
checkers.rationale: this is a purely internal consistency property of pymatgen's own orbit-construction arithmetic against the operation list it was itself handed; a violation would indicate either a bug in _unique_coords's deduplication (_site_tolerance too loose or too tight) or a symmetry_operations list that is not actually a closed group, either of which would silently produce a structure with the wrong site count, corrupting composition, density, and every downstream analysis of any structure parsed from that CIF
checkers.scientific_quantity: the size of the symmetry-equivalent orbit _unique_coords expands from a single asymmetric-unit coordinate under the CIF's parsed symmetry operations, which by the orbit-stabilizer theorem must evenly divide the number of parsed symmetry operations (len(orbit) = |G|/|stabilizer|)
